:::{#prp-pmf-density-counting}
#### A PMF is a density with respect to counting measure

If $X$ is a [discrete random variable](#def-discrete-rv) with [PMF](#def-pmf) $f_X$,
and $\measure$ is the [counting measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#def-counting-measure) on $\rangef{X}$,
then $f_X$ is a [density](#def-density-measure) of the distribution of $X$ with respect to $\measure$:
for every set $A \subseteq \rangef{X}$,

$$\Pr(X \in A) = \int_A f_X(x)\,d\measure(x)$$

:::

::: proof

The counting measure is defined on every subset of $\rangef{X}$,
so every function on $\rangef{X}$ is measurable,
and $f_X \ge 0$, because each of its values is a probability.
The range $\rangef{X}$ is countable, because $X$ is discrete,
so each $A \subseteq \rangef{X}$ is countable too,
and the event $\set{X \in A}$ is the union of the disjoint events $\set{X = x}$ for $x \in A$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(X \in A)
&= \sum_{x \in A} \Pr(X = x)
&& \text{(countable additivity)} \\
&= \sum_{x \in A} f_X(x)
&& \text{(definition of the PMF)} \\
&= \int_A f_X(x)\,d\measure(x)
&& \text{(an integral with respect to counting measure is a sum)}
\ea
$$

The first step is [countable additivity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#def-countable-additivity),
and the last is the [integral with respect to counting measure](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/measures.html#exm-integral-nonneg).

:::
